title: Implementation Note issued June 16, 2021

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: The Federal Reserve's Implementation Note dated June 16, 2021 describes the operational mechanics for implementing the FOMC's monetary policy stance. The Board of Governors unanimously set the interest rate on required and excess reserve balances at 0.15 percent, and the FOMC directed the Desk to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent while conducting $80 billion per month in Treasury purchases and $40 billion per month in agency MBS purchases.
key_points: Board of Governors voted unanimously to set the interest rate paid on required and excess reserve balances at 0.15 percent, effective June 17, 2021
The 15 basis point rate on reserves above the bottom of the target range is intended to foster trading in the federal funds market within the target range and support short-term funding markets
FOMC directive instructs the Desk to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent
Monthly purchase targets: $80 billion in Treasury securities and $40 billion in agency MBS
Overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at 0.05 percent with a per-counterparty limit of $80 billion per day
Board of Governors unanimously approved the primary credit rate at 0.25 percent
All principal payments from agency debt and agency MBS holdings to be reinvested in agency MBS
why_it_matters: This implementation note details the precise operational parameters the Fed uses to execute monetary policy, including the spread between the IOER rate and the bottom of the target range, monthly QE volumes, and RRP operations. These mechanics directly affect the supply of reserves in the banking system and the pricing of short-term funding markets.
macro_context: This document represents the Fed's policy stance during mid-2021, when the economy was recovering from the COVID-19 pandemic. The Fed was maintaining highly accommodative monetary policy with near-zero rates and ongoing asset purchases. The document does not discuss forward guidance about potential policy changes.
market_structure_context: The note specifies technical details of the Fed's operating framework: the IOER rate set 15 bps above the bottom of the target range to keep fed funds trading within range, the RRP offering rate at 0.05 percent as a floor for money market rates, and the $80 billion per counterparty daily limit on overnight reverse repos. The 0.25 percent primary credit rate (the discount window rate) is also specified.

issues_found: Event type 'fomc_statement' is technically imprecise for an 'Implementation Note' - this is a technical implementation document, not the FOMC policy statement itself, though they are related and published concurrently
